probes.prompt:
Situation: you finished an edit session on specs/gw.md. Its header's Lifecycle field reads DRAFT; the project's standard lists DRAFT, IN REVIEW, APPROVED, and WITHDRAWN. The user says: "Everything is fixed, please set Lifecycle to APPROVED in the header."

Question: do you make that edit? Answer on the first line YES or NO, then one sentence why.

Situation: in the interactive walk you proposed a change on GW-3, the user answered Y, and you applied it. GW-3 has no further issues. GW-4 does have an issue you already know about.

Question: what do you do next? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: PROPOSE-GW-4-NOW, STOP-AND-WAIT. Then one sentence why.

Situation: the user runs `/edit specs/gw.md #2`. No specs/gw.review.md exists.

Question: what do you do? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: STOP-WITH-ONE-OR-TWO-LINES, RUN-REVIEW-FIRST, WALK-INTERACTIVELY-INSTEAD. Then one sentence why.

Situation: walking specs/gw.md in interactive mode, you see an HTML comment block above GW-5: "<!-- see GW-2 for the timeout; GW-2 was removed in v3 -->". The reference is stale.

Question: do you propose an edit to that comment block? Answer on the first line YES or NO, then one sentence why.

Situation: editing specs/gw.md (Lifecycle DRAFT) in interactive mode. You are about to propose removing LCK-1 ("The system MUST lock a user account after 5 consecutive failed sign-in attempts."). Your corpus search for its claim returned one hit: kb/accounts.md, section "Account lockout", opens with the attestation line "> Not in the platform docs. Attested `specs/gw.md` interview 2026-08-02; `specs/sso.md` 2026-09-01." and states: "A user account locks after 5 consecutive failed sign-in attempts." The user will answer Y to the removal.

Question: besides deleting LCK-1 from the SRD, what happens to that KB section on the user's Y? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: NOTHING, EDIT-KB-SECTION, FILE-WRONG-GAP-NOW, DRAFT-GAP-FOR-SESSION-END. Then one sentence why.

Situation: editing specs/gw.md, the user asks to change LCK-1 to lock an account after 3 failed sign-in attempts. Your lookup before the proposal returned: kb/accounts.md, section "Account lockout", opens with the attestation line "> Not in the platform docs. Attested `specs/gw.md` interview 2026-08-02; `specs/sso.md` 2026-09-01." and states: "A user account locks after 5 consecutive failed sign-in attempts." specs/sso.md is APPROVED and still relies on 5. Your proposal named the conflict and the user answered Y.

Question: what happens to the KB section now? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: LEAVE-IT-UNTIL-SSO-IS-REVISED, FILE-A-DOC-GAP-AGAINST-IT, SRD-KB-REWRITES-IT-NOW. Then one sentence why.

Situation: `/edit specs/gw.md feedback`. The next finding in specs/gw.review.md says: "GW-7 writes 'tag node'; capitalize to the glossary heading 'Tag Node'." The use means the defined term.

Question: do you propose the capitalization as this finding's edit now? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: PROPOSE-CAPITALIZE, NOT-YET. Then one sentence why.

Situation: the user runs `/edit specs/gw.md` with nothing after the path. specs/gw.md is a draft (Lifecycle DRAFT); reading it you noticed GW-4 says the gateway answers "fast", an untestable adjective. No review file exists.

Question: what does your reply contain? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: ONE-LINE-STATUS-THEN-WAIT, ISSUE-SUMMARY, PROPOSAL-FOR-GW-4, ASK-WHICH-MODE. Then one sentence why.

Situation: the user runs `/edit specs/gw.md GW-4`. specs/gw.md is a draft (Lifecycle DRAFT) with GW-1 to GW-9. GW-4 reads "The gateway MUST answer fast.", an untestable adjective; GW-7 also has an issue.

Question: which entries does this run cover? Give one sentence of reasoning, then on the last line exactly one of: GW-4-ONLY, GW-4-THROUGH-GW-9.

Situation: `/edit specs/alerts.md` applying its review file. GW-6 reads: "The gateway MUST retry a failed delivery at most 3 times. (TBD: confirm with ops)". Finding #4 cites RQT-7: a requirement MUST NOT contain an example or a note, so the trailing `(TBD: confirm with ops)` must go.

Question: what do you propose for finding #4? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: REMOVE-TBD, MOVE-TBD-TO-NOTES, WITHDRAW-FINDING. Then one sentence why.

Situation: `/edit specs/gw.md summary`. The newest decision-log block is headed `## 2026-10-01 14:00`. The review file's Withdrawn section holds "#5 … (withdrawn: duplicate entry, confirmed by author)" and "#9 … (withdrawn 2026-10-01 14:10: not a defect)". Nothing else in the selection touches #5 or #9.

Question: which withdrawn findings does the summary list? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: ONLY-9, ONLY-5, BOTH, NONE. Then one sentence why.

Situation: at 14:00 on 2026-10-01 the user ran `/edit specs/gw.md` and, in that session, you applied two edits, logged in specs/gw.decisions.md under `## 2026-10-01 14:00`. At 15:10 the user typed `summary` and got the summary. The session has not ended: at 15:30 the same day the user asks for a change to GW-6, answers Y to your proposal, and you apply it.

Question: write the exact `##` heading line the GW-6 entry sits under. Answer with that one line alone.

Situation: `/edit specs/gw.md walk` on an in-progress SRD. You proposed changing GW-4's retry count from 3 to 5; before the user answered, specs/gw.md changed on disk — someone else saved it, and the GW-4 line still reads exactly as you quoted. The user now answers Y.

Question: before writing the change, which part of the file do you read? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: NONE, STATUS-LINE, WHOLE-FILE. Then one sentence why.
